children: The head of Russia’s biggest lender said his country’s central bank is working with the Reserve Bank of India on a mechanism to use digital currencies to settle bilateral trade, in what would be a breakthrough for making cross-border payments faster and more efficient.

“Now it’s only beginning, but we see huge opportunity for digital currency for all settlements between the countries,” Sberbank Chief Executive Officer Herman Gref told reporters in New Delhi, where India is hosting the annual summit of the BRICS group of nations. Speaking on Friday, he added that the digital currencies would see greater demand and faster growth.

Russia rolled out its central bank digital currency — the digital ruble — on Sept. 1 through systemically significant banks including state-controlled Sberbank. India launched its digital currency on a pilot basis in 2022, and it’s now used in some government programs as well.
“The Russian central bank and the central bank of India are working on this very precisely and we have tried to support them because we need this kind of instrument,” Gref said.

The Kremlin said Thursday that Russia would discuss the use of digital currencies for trade settlements with BRICS members and partner nations at this week’s summit in New Delhi, an initiative India has also backed.
The RBI didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment after Gref’s remarks.

With India chairing BRICS this year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi favors using central bank digital currencies to settle bilateral trade between members and cross-border payments, without positioning the initiative as a challenge to the dollar.

BRICS members have been working toward linking their payment systems in ways that could reduce reliance on the global SWIFT network, which is dominated by Western nations. The initiative gained attention after many major Russian banks were cut off from SWIFT following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

On Russian companies’ accumulation of rupees in vostro accounts - which foreign banks hold with Indian lenders to settle trade in the rupee — Gref said the issue was no longer a significant challenge because firms had found “the right ways to utilize all the rupees.”

“Now it’s not the problem in our trade and we try to increase the trade between the countries,” he said. He also said that some of the excessive rupees have been invested in the federal government securities, without providing a figure.

Russia accumulated billions of dollars in rupees in India as trade between the countries jumped after President Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. To enable Russia to use the accumulated rupees, the Reserve Bank of India came up with rules allowing these funds to be invested in projects or Indian securities, as well as to pay for future purchases of goods and services.
India and Russia have been among each other’s top five trading partners since 2022, when India stepped up its purchases of Russian oil.

Bilateral trade totaled nearly $60 billion, with the bulk being India’s imports of Russian oil, in India’s fiscal 2026. While the two countries aim to expand bilateral trade to $100 billion by the end of the decade, India currently imports far more from Russia than it exports.
“We need to bring more Indian exports and more opportunities to the Russian market and this is our goal,” Gref said, adding that the over $50-billion trade imbalance needs to be corrected.

title: Russia, India explore digital currencies for trade settlements, says Sberbank CEO Herman Gref
